extracted.intended_audience: USPTO staff (examiners, OPQA reviewers, TC managers) and external stakeholders (patent applicants, policymakers) interested in how patent examination quality is measured
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO guidance describing how the Agency measures and evaluates patent examination quality via statutory compliance, process, and perception metrics; explains OPQA sampling and review methods, the Master Review Form, metric calculations, and survey design/validation. Intended to govern assessment of Office actions and broader quality-improvement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality patent (USPTO definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality patent is one that is correctly issued in compliance with all the requirements of Title 35 as well as the relevant case law at the time of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality work product includes appropriate and clear patentability determinations for every pending claim throughout prosecution; USPTO focuses on continuous quality improvement and efficiency to support issuance of quality patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part quality metrics approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's quality metrics approach includes a focus on: (1) statutory compliance measures; (2) process measures; and (3) perception measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each focus area has distinct measurement methods (OPQA random reviews for compliance, monitoring/root-cause/process measures, and internal/external surveys for perception) and together provide a thorough understanding of patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling for OPQA random reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA randomly reviews Office actions to generate statutory compliance measures; the random sample is representative by Office action type and technology-type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal in recent years: ~10,000 work product reviews per fiscal year. OPQA randomizes Office actions mailed within a prior seven-day period to create a pull list and assigns reviewers based on technology area so sample represents non-final rejection, final rejection, allowance, and technology distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory compliance standard (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA reviews Office actions for statutory compliance by evaluating whether the Office action includes appropriate and clear determinations for every pending claim based on the patentability statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review evaluates each claim under each relevant statute; a single improper or omitted determination for any claim renders the entire Office action noncompliant. Rebuttal and reconsideration processes exist between OPQA and the TC.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. §102 — Novelty evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions are evaluated for correct determinations under 35 U.S.C. §102 (Novelty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the statutory compliance review: ensure rejections under §102 are correct, identify the claim and statute, and set forth sufficient evidence to put a person skilled in the art on notice why the claim is unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. §103 — Non-Obviousness evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions are evaluated for correct determinations under 35 U.S.C. §103 (Non-Obviousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA checks that obviousness rejections are properly supported and explained so a person skilled in the art is put on notice; omission of a proper §103 rejection yields noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. §112 — Specification (Enablement, Written Description, Definiteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions are evaluated for correct determinations under 35 U.S.C. §112 covering enablement, written description, and definiteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether §112-related rejections are correct and sufficiently explained; omissions or improper determinations under §112 render the Office action noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. §101 — Subject Matter Eligibility and Utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions are evaluated for correct determinations under 35 U.S.C. §101 (Inventions Patentable: Subject Matter Eligibility, Utility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA ensures §101 determinations are appropriate and clearly explained; failure to make a required §101 rejection or making an incorrect §101 determination affects compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum content required in a rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with the statutory compliance standard, rejections must be correct and must, at a minimum, appropriately (1) identify the claim and relevant statute and (2) set forth sufficient evidence to put a person skilled in the art on notice as to why the claim is considered unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient explanation or omission of the claim/statute or supporting evidence leads to a finding of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted rejection is noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to make a rejection under a statutory basis that should have been made (i.e., omitted rejection) results in the work product not complying with the statutory compliance standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA treats omitted rejections as noncompliant findings; such findings are verified by an OPQA supervisor and sent to the relevant TC for consideration and possible rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Review Form (MRF) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers in OPQA and the Technology Centers use the Master Review Form (MRF) — a modular review form — to evaluate work product for statutory compliance and other prosecution quality areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MRF includes over 20 sections and a 330+ question library; updated (FY2020) to include 'Characteristics' sections to capture best practices and Office action clarity; serves as the basis for awarding accolades for high-quality work product that go beyond MPEP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review flow principle: claim-by-claim, statute-by-statute evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating work product under the statutory compliance standard, OPQA reviewers evaluate how an Office action addresses every claim under each statute to ensure proper rejections and that no proper rejections were omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because every claim is reviewed under each statute, many statutory compliance evaluations are performed per Office action. If any single claim has an improper determination under any statute, the entire Office action is identified as noncompliant regardless of other correct determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance metric calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The compliance metric is calculated by dividing the total number of Office actions that properly evaluated all pending claims in light of the patentability statutes by the total number of Office actions reviewed; expressed as a percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics can be broken down by relevant statute. Results are validated through TC feedback, comparisons to TC-performed reviews, and external perception survey data. OPQA monitors consistency of its reviews and does not set targets/incentives based on noncompliance findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and rebuttal of OPQA findings
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA's noncompliance findings are verified by an OPQA supervisor and sent to the relevant Technology Center for consideration; the TC may file a rebuttal and OPQA has a process to reconsider findings based on arguments presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance metrics are validated in part through TC feedback and comparison to other review sources; this feedback loop supports metric accuracy and follow-on corrective actions or training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process measures focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Process measures track efficiency and consistency of examination processes with a focus on preventing reopening of prosecution, reducing rework, and ensuring consistency of decision-making that results in impeccable work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO conducts root-cause analysis on trends and behaviors to capture best practices or correct issues; process measures inform training and operational changes to improve quality and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring data sources and examiner benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO leverages data sources such as PALM and the MRF to identify trends and examiner behaviors; examiners are provided on-demand access to their own statistics for benchmarking against art unit, TC, and corps averages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring provides consistency data to supervisors and helps identify behaviors indicative of best practices or potential quality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception measures: internal and external surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception measures include semi-annual internal and external stakeholder surveys that provide vital indicators of quality and validate other USPTO quality metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal survey: sent to 750 randomly selected patent examiners; focuses on factors impacting examiners' ability to provide high-quality examination (tools, training, coaching, incoming applications, applicant interactions). External survey: sent to 3,000 frequent-filing customers; focuses on customer perspectives on correctness, clarity, and consistency of rejections, adherence to rules/procedures, satisfaction with search/prior art, and includes a rotating panel design and one open-ended question each enumeration. Surveys are administered/ analyzed by a third-party under the Chief Statistician's guidance to maintain objectivity and anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other targeted reviews and partnerships with TCs
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to random reviews, OPQA conducts numerous other reviews throughout each fiscal year often in partnership with Technology Centers to investigate specific quality issues relevant to stakeholders or TC needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted reviews allow deeper investigation of particular issues, validation of trends, and development of tailored corrective or best-practice recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accolade designation for high-quality work product
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA reviewers identify high-quality work product with an accolade for including best practices that go beyond the requirements of the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MRF 'Characteristics' sections capture information about use of best practices and Office action clarity; accolades are based on those characteristics and highlight exemplary work for coaching and recognition purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling corrections for finalized noncompliant work product
rubrics_metrics.description: When OPQA finalizes that work product is noncompliant, the appropriate course of correction is left to the Technology Center; for allowances, this includes correction prior to issuing the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA provides findings to the TC, and the TC determines corrective action; the process includes verification, rebuttal, and reconsideration steps before final resolution.
